subject: body
title: Food Is Fuel
about: Why we eat: food is the body's fuel for running, thinking and growing, different foods do different jobs (go foods for energy, builder foods, protecting foods), the hungry and full signals, why breakfast wakes up the brain, fuel being used even in sleep, water as part of the fuel, and where food's energy first came from (the sun). NC 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them) and 1.NPA.1.1 (reasons to drink water); the first level of Healthy Eating. Read it together: the tablet reads every card aloud, and you add what was on his plate today.
tip: Before a meal, ask him how his fuel tank feels: empty, half full or full. Ask again at the end.

cards.q: A car needs gas to go. What does your body need to go?
cards.note: Food is your body's fuel. It gives you the energy to run, think and grow.

cards.q: Food is like fuel. What does fuel do for a car or a body?
cards.note: Fuel is what makes something go. Gas for the car, food for you.

cards.q: Food does three big jobs. It gives you energy, helps you think, and helps you...?
cards.note: Every day your body builds new bone, skin and muscle. Food brings the building blocks.

cards.q: Bread, rice and pasta are go foods. What do go foods give you?
cards.note: Go foods are grains: bread, rice, oats, pasta and tortillas. They are the quickest way to fill your energy tank.

cards.q: Protein foods like eggs and beans are the builders. What do they build?
cards.note: Builder foods are protein: eggs, beans, fish, chicken, nuts and tofu. They build and fix your body.

cards.q: Grains give energy and protein builds. What job do fruits and vegetables do?
cards.note: Fruits and vegetables carry vitamins that protect your eyes, your skin and your germ fighters.

cards.q: Your tummy rumbles and feels empty. What is your body saying?
cards.note: A rumbling, empty tummy is your hunger signal. It means it is time to eat.

cards.q: You are eating dinner and your tummy starts to feel full. What do you do?
cards.note: Full means the tank is topped up. You can stop, even if some food is left on the plate.

cards.q: Who knows best if you are hungry or full?
cards.note: Listen to your body. Eat when it says hungry and stop when it says full.

cards.q: You slept all night with no food. What does breakfast do for your brain?
cards.note: Breakfast gives your brain fresh fuel to think, listen and learn at school.

cards.q: You skip lunch. By the afternoon, how might you feel?
cards.note: An empty tank makes it hard to think and play nicely. Meals keep your energy steady.

cards.q: Plants make their food from sunlight, and we eat plants. So where did food's energy first come from?
cards.note: Plants catch sunlight to make their food. We eat plants, or animals that ate plants, so the energy in your lunch started as sunshine.

cards.q: Your brain works best when you drink enough...?
cards.note: Water is part of your fuel too. Every part of you, even your thinking, needs it.

cards.q: You sleep all night long. Does your body use fuel while you sleep?
cards.note: Even asleep, your heart beats, you breathe and you grow, and all of that uses fuel. That is why you wake up ready for breakfast.

cards.q: Your tummy is like a fuel tank. It empties as you play. When does it fill back up?
cards.note: Playing, thinking and growing all use fuel. Meals and snacks fill the tank again.

cards.q: Reading and math make your brain work hard. What does your brain run on?
cards.note: Your brain uses lots of energy, even when you sit still. That is one more reason to eat breakfast.

cards.q: Who needs fuel from food every single day?
cards.note: Kids, grown-ups and grandparents all need food every day. Growing kids use lots of fuel.
